text:
Palestinian student Mahdi Tounsi appeared in a closed-door court hearing in Jerusalem, as academics and activists warned that Israel’s attempt to jail him without trial marked a serious escalation in attacks on Palestinian rights.
Yael Berda, a lawyer and sociology professor at Hebrew University, who has taught Tounsi for four years, came to court to call for his release.
“I have no doubt this is a case of political persecution based on identity and political activity,” she said outside the courtroom. “Mehdi’s arrest is part of a campaign that we’ve seen very much escalating since the elections.”
Her student was “almost unrecognisable” when he appeared on a video link in the courtroom, deprived of his glasses, with his hair and beard shaved and with visible bruising, she added.
Tounsi, a sociology and criminology student at Hebrew University in Jerusalem, was seized from his dorm on 8 November. He is held at Megiddo prison where documented abuse includes starvation rations, violent attacks on prisoners and rampant scabies and other diseases.
Thousands of Palestinians from the occupied West Bank are held under administrative detention orders but they have rarely been used against Palestinians who have Israeli citizenship or residence status in occupied East Jerusalem.
Prison authorities had not complied with a judge’s order to return Tounsi’s glasses, his brief public appearance on Tuesday showed.
Israeli prosecutors are seeking an administrative detention order, which allows for up to six months’ detention without trial or public presentation of evidence.
Security forces presented a summary of evidence in a hearing closed even to Tounsi and his lawyers, making a defence effectively impossible.
Tounsi’s arrest comes amid a racist campaign of delegitimisation against Palestinian citizens of Israel, whose votes were critical to stripping Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition of its majority in elections last month.
Noa Dagoni, executive director of Jerusalem-focused rights group Ir Amin, described Tounsi’s arrest as a dangerous escalation in political persecution of activists, particularly those “at the junction of human rights, dialogue and non-violent action”.
Many of the Ir Amin staff count Tounsi as a personal friend after years working together in his home community of Silwan, where Israeli authorities are forcing mass displacements of Palestinians, including to make way for a theme park.
Dagoni fears he may have been targeted for this work. “We’re very concerned that this [arrest] has to do with his being a non-violent peace activist, also dealing with the displacement in his community,” she said.
“The partnership of Israelis and Palestinians is very intimidating for this government because it can be effective, it can build real political power.”
Officers from the Shin Bet security force failed to appear in court to present evidence at a first hearing last week, so the judge reconvened on Tuesday.
Reflecting concern about the case, his family and lawyer were joined in the courthouse by prominent activists, Knesset member Ofer Cassif, diplomats from Ireland, the Netherlands and the EU, his tutor and the dean of students from Hebrew University.
Hundreds of Jewish and Palestinian demonstrators gathered in the street outside calling for his immediate release.
Many knew Tounsi personally from classes or activism, including Lana, a Palestinian citizen of Israel.
“Someone who I know being kidnapped was really frightening,” she said. “It makes me think of my place here also, how it might affect me and if there are more people who I know who are going to be arrested soon.”
Many protesters were angry with university authorities, including Arielle, 27, a former student at the same campus. “Israeli universities need to take accountability for this, like they can’t allow students to be kidnapped from their dorm rooms,” she said.
Hebrew University’s dean of students, Zohar Kampf, said the university asked to testify but its request was rejected. The university has not commented on Tounsi’s violent arrest, deprivation of glasses and other mistreatment.
Cassif, the Knesset member, called for a global pressure campaign. “Where is the international community, especially academia. What are they waiting for?” he said. “Speak up, do something, raise your voice.”
The police did not respond to questions about visible marks of abuse or details of the case against Tounsi. A spokesperson said: “The suspect was lawfully arrested as part of an investigation conducted by the Jerusalem District Central Investigations Unit concerning ties to an act of terrorism.”
